summary.name: Cartography
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article covering the history, theory, and map types of cartography, the study and practice of making and using maps.
use_cases: Understanding map projections and their distortions
Studying map bias and critical cartography
summary.what_it_does: The article describes cartography as combining science, aesthetics and technique to model reality so spatial information can be communicated. It outlines the core objectives of traditional mapmaking, including map editing, projections, generalization and map design. It traces the history of maps from ancient artifacts and medieval mappae mundi through Renaissance printing methods such as woodcut and copper-plate intaglio, the Mercator projection, and early modern atlases. It also covers modern digital cartography, the difference between general and thematic maps, and critical readings of map bias, including imperialism in Africa.
notable: Covers ancient to modern map history, from Babylonian world maps to digital GIS
Explains Renaissance woodcut and intaglio printing techniques
Discusses deconstruction and bias in maps, including the Mercator projection and Africa
